thinkingMap.title: Handover between shifts at a small veterinary practice
thinkingMap.seedIdea: Our vets lose things between the morning and evening shift — a dog that needed re-checking, an owner who was promised a call back. Everyone blames the whiteboard but I don't think the whiteboard is the problem.

message.content: Our vets lose things between the morning and evening shift — a dog that needed re-checking, an owner who was promised a call back. Everyone blames the whiteboard but I don't think the whiteboard is the problem.

Agreed that the whiteboard is probably a symptom. Three things worth pulling apart: what specifically falls through, who is meant to be carrying it at the moment it falls, and only then what shape a fix would take.
The call-backs are the ones that sting. A missed re-check we catch the next day. A missed call-back we hear about in a review.

mapNode.label: Handover between shifts at a small veterinary practice
mapNode.detail: Our vets lose things between the morning and evening shift — a dog that needed re-checking, an owner who was promised a call back.

mapNode.label: Which handover item goes missing most often?
mapNode.detail: Owner call-backs. A missed re-check surfaces the next morning; a missed call-back surfaces in a public review three weeks later.

mapNode.label: At what moment does it actually get dropped?
mapNode.choices: ["During the verbal handover", "After handover, before the task is done", "It was never written down at all"]

mapNode.label: The whiteboard is wiped at 6pm, before the evening shift has read it
mapNode.detail: Photographed on two consecutive Tuesdays. The evening vet arrives at 6:15.
mapNode.imageAlt: A wall-mounted whiteboard covered in handwritten notes, half of it wiped clean.

mapNode.label: Who is supposed to own a call-back once the shift ends?
mapNode.choices: ["The vet who promised it", "Whoever is on the evening desk", "Nobody — it is on the board"]

mapNode.label: The receptionist is already the informal handover system
mapNode.detail: She remembers what the board does not, which is why nobody has felt the gap as a system problem yet.

mapNode.label: A handover list that survives the shift boundary
mapNode.detail: Each open promise carries an owner and does not clear itself until someone closes it.
mapNode.diagram: {"steps": ["Vet promises a call-back", "It joins the open list with their name on it", "Evening shift sees it unclosed", "Closing it needs a person, not a wipe"], "note": "The wipe is what deletes the state today."}

mapNode.label: A second screen nobody looks at during a busy consult
mapNode.detail: The whiteboard's one real virtue is that it is in the room and always visible.

mapNode.label: Does this replace the whiteboard or sit beside it?
Call-backs only, for one week, on paper
mapNode.detail: If a named owner and an explicit close fixes call-backs on paper, the software is worth building. If it does not, no screen will save it.
